column1: # Placement of WORKLIST_A against the faceted models ontology (MODELS_AXES.md).
# One row per input name. Columns:
#   name        -- the corpus string, verbatim from WORKLIST_A.tsv
#   verdict     -- lineage | alias | generic | algorithm | quarantine | misextraction | unsure
#   target      -- lineage: the R1 PARENT node_id (| separates R5 second parents).
#                  alias: the node_id it spells. Otherwise empty.
#   connectivity / topology / attributes -- for `lineage`, ONLY what the node pins
#                  beyond what resolve.py already gives its parent; for `generic`,
#                  everything the NAME ALONE pins. node_ids, | separated.
#   why         -- the rule or framing that decides it

column8: why
Contrastive SSL objective over an unchanged backbone; settled algorithm-side by the backbone test.
Self-distillation SSL objective with an EMA target; the encoder is an unchanged ResNet/ViT. Same class as SimCLR.
Value-learning algorithm; settled algorithm-side. The network it trains is a plain CNN or MLP.
Redundancy-reduction SSL objective on a joint-embedding pair; backbone unchanged.
Maximum-entropy off-policy RL algorithm; the actor and critic are generic MLPs.

Released ViT checkpoints that papers execute; DINOv2 is already a node under ViT, so its predecessor release is treated the same. The self-distillation objective itself is algorithm-side. Pins nothing beyond ViT. See notes: DINO/DINOv2/MAE/V-JEPA are the same judgement call (L-18).
GFlowNet is settled algorithm-side: a training procedure for a sequential sampler; the sampler is an arbitrary backbone.
Uninformative generic, quarantined exactly as the brief's 4.7 row and as `machine learning` was in the domains design.
PPO; settled algorithm-side.
R1: the paper's own expansion is `GeomEtry-Aware Relational Graph Neural Network`, so the GNN edge is a framing claim. Relational edge-type message passing refines the parent's `Message passing`.
Offline RL objective (a Q-value regulariser); leaves the network unchanged.
R3: a separately named release under GPT-3.5, not a spelling of it. Pins nothing new. Proposed node_id gpt35_turbo; `gpt-3.5 turbo` in this same worklist is its orthographic alias.
R3 case 2: long form plus declared acronym of the root node `Feedforward network (multilayer perceptron)`. `multilayer perceptron` is already in SPELLINGS.tsv at priority 1.

Decoder-only code LLM. Its literal R1 parent is StarCoderBase (`we fine-tuned StarCoderBase ... resulting in StarCoder`), which is not a node; `Transformer` is the nearest existing descent parent. Topology must be pinned because the Transformer root deliberately pins none (L-10).
A generic description. Depth and width are paper facts, not axis values; the name alone pins only a dense feedforward net.

MODELS_AXES is explicit: `Autoencoder` is neither a lineage node nor a topology value. The name pins encoder-decoder topology and a deterministic latent; the reconstruction target is the algorithms-dimension residue.
Autoregressive code LLM released as its own family (350M/2B/6B/16B). Same shape as StarCoder.
`pre-train a protein encoder by sequence-structure joint diffusion modeling` -- an objective over an unchanged encoder. Diffusion is settled algorithm-side.
A GFlowNet variant for cyclic causal structures; GFlowNet is settled algorithm-side. The paper calls it an architecture, and its hypernetwork sampler is architectural -- flagged in notes.
R1: `FAENet: a simple, fast and expressive GNN`. Deliberately drops symmetry-preserving constraints, which is the symmetry default, so nothing to pin there.
R3: a separately named release of GPT-4 (vision). No axis value for input modality, so it pins nothing -- see notes.
Diffusion is settled algorithm-side. Its architectural content is an attention mask derived from problem structure, which is attributes=sparse-attention on a Transformer backbone, not a new lineage.

A learned optimizer. Is a parameterised optimizer a model (the authors call LAgg-A an architecture, and it is a small network with its own wiring) or part of the training procedure, i.e. algorithm-side? The design rules do not decide this, and the answer governs a whole class of learned-optimization names.
Same question as LAgg-A: the worker-invariant learned optimizer from the same paper. Model-side or algorithm-side is undecided by the current rules.
BOUNDARY_CASES L-24 already defers this one by name: no vendor architecture statement exists, so a parent would be a guess. Left for a design pass, not resolved here.
R3 case 1+2: hyphenation variant of the long form plus the declared acronym.
RapidBrachyMCTPS is Monte Carlo brachytherapy treatment-planning software, not a learned model. Same class of defect as `pytorch`.
`Siamese Diffusion Trajectory Prediction`, a pretraining method that enhances DiffPreT; an objective over an unchanged protein encoder.
A task-defined class (predicting a species' niche), realised as GLMs, MaxEnt or random forests. It pins nothing on any model axis; what it names belongs to the task/domain dimension. See notes.
Swapped-assignment clustering SSL objective; backbone unchanged.
R3: a separately named release (size + patch size). Size variants are nodes, never aliases. Pins nothing beyond ViT.
`Adaptive-eta`, a learning-rate adaptation module -- squarely optimization, algorithm-side. The trailing character was lost in extraction (see notes).
A named application system (a monkeypox image detector). Neither the name nor the quote states an architecture, so any R1 parent would be a guess. Is it a model release at all, or a deployed system?
A named code-generation model; DeepMind describes an encoder-decoder Transformer. Topology pinned because the Transformer root pins none.
An open-source agent framework that calls a language model; it is software, not a learned model. If agent scaffolding is wanted as a concept it is algorithm-side, not models[].

BOUNDARY_CASES L-20 deleted this from lineage: it is attributes=bayesian-weights on whatever lineage the paper names. The connectivity comes from the paper, not from the name. SPELLINGS.tsv header calls out the wrong `Bayesian network` pairing explicitly.
An opponent-shaping training approach for multi-agent RL; it changes who the agent trains against, not the network.
Google's Switch-style sparse model family evaluated in BIG-bench, named and reported as a distinct family from dense BIG-G. MoE routing is the pin that separates it.
Bootstrapped Meta-Gradients: a meta-gradient training procedure; the agent architecture is unchanged.
Categorical/distributional Q-learning; a change of the learning target, not the network.

The ChatGPT product on its GPT-3.5 backend; the quote uses bare `ChatGPT`. Ambiguous between the `ChatGPT` and `GPT-3.5` nodes, which L-24 keeps separate -- flagged in notes rather than claimed as certain.
An optimizer (gradient clipping + SGD). Optimizers are algorithm-side; one landing in models[] is the mirror of adam landing in libraries[].
Clipped Stochastic Similar Triangles Method -- an accelerated optimizer.
An exploration procedure for RL; leaves the network unchanged.
Self-described: `a new RL algorithm ... can be added to any existing RL algorithm`. That is the backbone test's definition of algorithm-side.

Not one name: a retriever-plus-reader pipeline string. It should be split into Contriever (a BERT-family dense retriever, no node yet) and Flan-T5 (already a node). The verdict set has no value for a composite configuration string -- see notes.

A named design (cooperative Concept Bottleneck Model), but its R1 parent is `Concept bottleneck model`, which does not exist in lineage. R7 forbids me creating that grouping/family node, so this is flagged for a design pass rather than attached to a backbone it does not descend from.
Self-described: `a new algorithm for planning as inference` built from sequential Monte Carlo plus learned heuristic factors -- a sampling procedure.
A GFlowNet for crystal structures; GFlowNet is settled algorithm-side. What is new is the state/action space and reward, not a network design.

A transformer world model plus policy over discrete (codebook) tokens. Read as a named architecture it is a Transformer child; read as `a sample-efficient method` (its own words) it is algorithm-side. Low confidence, flagged.
R3 case 2: long form plus declared acronym of the existing node.
DQN; settled algorithm-side. Long-form spelling of the same algorithm, but with no lineage node to alias to, the verdict is the algorithm verdict.
DQN again, singular/hyphenated. Algorithm-side.
Diffusion is settled algorithm-side; DDPM is the canonical formulation. The network it trains is a U-Net.
Direct Epistemic Uncertainty Prediction: a framework that fits a secondary error predictor. The secondary predictor is an unconstrained backbone; what is named is the estimation procedure.
A framework for estimating epistemic uncertainty in diffusion models by ensembling; both ingredients are algorithm-side. Residue: the ensembling is topology=ensemble on whatever backbone is used.

Object-centric model: Slot Attention over frozen DINO ViT features with feature reconstruction. R1 names slot attention; an R5 second parent (ViT/DINO) is arguable since the encoder is frozen and supplies the features the slots bind to.

A one-layer linear forecaster with trend/seasonal decomposition, introduced as the LTSF-Linear family. Pins nothing new: Linear model already gives fully-connected + single component. The decomposition front end has no axis value.
Same defect as `contriever + flan-t5`: a two-model pipeline string (DPR retriever + Fusion-in-Decoder reader), neither of which is a node yet. Needs splitting, not a verdict.
Data-regularized Q: image augmentation plus Q-learning; the network is unchanged.

Self-described `encoder-decoder model for continuous-time dynamic graphs`, built on attention-based message passing over temporal neighbourhoods. The temporal-graph aspect has no axis value (see notes).
A representation-learning model over dynamic graphs: neighbourhood propagation driven by a temporal point process. The point-process part is a training objective; the wiring is message passing.
A graphical user interface for a Monte Carlo dose engine. Software, not a model -- the name says so.

`an equivariant model that directly predicts the coordinates of the docked pose` -- an SE(3)-equivariant graph matching network. EGNN is a plausible R5/R1 alternative parent. Topology deliberately left inherited: the two graphs exchange messages at every layer, so `multi-tower` (combined only at the end) does not apply.

Feature-wise Linear Modulation is a conditioning layer, not a model and not a training procedure. L-06 states conditioning schemes are not lineage, but nothing in the design says where they go, and no axis has a value for conditioning. See notes.
`a scalable force-centric GNN that does not impose explicit physical constraints` -- R1 names GNN, and the explicit non-equivariance is the symmetry default, so there is nothing to pin.

Residual Gated Graph ConvNet (Bresson & Laurent). The quote itself notes the residual connections, which is the attribute pin. `gcn` is a possible alternative parent; the paper frames it from graph ConvNets plus edge gates.
R3 case 2: acronym plus long form of the existing GCN node.
R3: a separately named release. The technical report describes it as a sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer, which is the one pin that differs from the Gemini parent.
Long form of GFlowNet; settled algorithm-side, so it resolves to the algorithm, not to an alias.
Self-described `SE(3)-invariant denoising distance matching pretraining algorithm` -- an objective over an unchanged molecular encoder.

Graph HyperNetwork (third generation): a GNN over a network's computational graph that predicts another network's parameters. The GNN edge is R1-grounded, but the axes have no value for a hypernetwork (a model whose output is another model's weights) -- see notes. Its true R1 parent GHN-2 is absent.

`an evolution of the SciML generative model GOKU-nets`: a VAE whose latent evolves under a learned ODE/SDE. Its literal R1 parent GOKU-net is absent, and Neural ODE is the natural R5 second parent but would wrongly import `standard convolution` (see notes). Latent-ODE dynamics have no connectivity value.

A product name, which L-24 admits as a node under the family vendor documentation supports -- Google documents a Transformer NMT system since 2020. But the served system changed backbone (GNMT was LSTM-based), so this pin is time-dependent in a way the other L-24 products are not.
R3 case 1: orthographic variant (space vs hyphen) of `gpt-3.5-turbo`, which this same file admits as a node under GPT-3.5. Target is that proposed node_id.
R3: a separately named release in the GPT-4 generation. No axis value for the omni/multimodal interface, so it pins nothing.
An optimizer. Belongs to the deferred algorithms dimension; it is not a model under any reading.
R3 case 2: the long form of GCN.
R3 cases 2+3: plural of the long form of GCN.
Self-described `model-agnostic and task-agnostic` unsupervised method for discovering steerable factors -- model-agnostic is the backbone test passing out loud.
A regulariser on the support of the learned representation (a disentanglement criterion); it changes the objective, not the network.
A multi-agent training scheme over PPO; algorithm-side.

A released instruction-tuned vision-language model. Instruction tuning is algorithm-side, but the released artifact is a node, exactly as Vicuna and Alpaca are nodes under LLaMA. Its literal R1 parent is BLIP-2, which is missing (see notes).

The quote states the design: a conditional variational recurrent neural network followed by a kinematic model. There is no `Variational RNN` family, so the stochastic latent and encoder-decoder shape are pinned directly on a Recurrent network child. The bicycle kinematic model is a non-learned component the axes cannot express.
Unbalanced mini-batch optimal transport for domain adaptation; the quote itself calls the set it belongs to `PDA algorithms`.

R1 by name and by framing: a decoder-only foundation model for probabilistic time-series forecasting built on the LLaMA architecture. Pins nothing new -- the lag-feature tokenization and the distributional output head are input/output choices no axis carries (see notes).
R1: `a new computationally efficient sub-quadratic NP variant`. The latent bottleneck is a fixed set of latent vectors read by cross-attention, which the parent does not have.
R3 case 2: long form plus acronym of the existing node. Note this is LDA-the-discriminant, not LDA-the-topic-model -- both exist in lineage and the acronym is shared (see notes).
A GFlowNet training procedure that adds local search in object space; explicitly a training-effectiveness change.
R3 case 2: long form plus declared acronym of the existing LSTM node.
A named many-to-many multilingual translation model release; encoder-decoder Transformer.
Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning -- model-agnostic by name; a training procedure over any backbone.
Diffusion applied to 3D meshes via deformable tetrahedral grids. Diffusion is settled algorithm-side; the denoiser is a 3D U-Net.
A meta-learning procedure built on a surrogate meta-value function; the networks are unchanged.
A data-augmentation/regularization scheme (an improvement of Mixup); nothing in the network changes.

`Kitchen Sinks` in the expanded name is literal: random convolutional features followed by ridge regression, i.e. random-feature kernel ridge. The convolution pin is the random featurizer. Low confidence -- `Linear model` is a defensible alternative parent if the random features are read as preprocessing rather than as the model.

A diffusion generative model that co-generates 2D graph and 3D geometry; diffusion is settled algorithm-side. Its MUformer denoiser is a Transformer/GNN hybrid that could be a node if the owner wants denoiser architectures admitted.

column1: multi-headed bayesian deep learning probabilistic model
column8: A generic description, not a named design. It pins Bayesian weights; `multi-headed` (one trunk, several output heads) has no axis value -- see notes.
R3: a separately named size release under OPT. Size variants are nodes, never aliases.
Partial Adversarial Domain Adaptation; the quote groups it with `PDA algorithms`. A training scheme, not an architecture.
PopulAtion Parameter Averaging -- a weight-averaging training method; the models averaged keep their architecture.
R3/R1: a separately named release that adds an output-query cross-attention decoder, which is the topology pin. Note the parent Perceiver currently resolves to NO topology at all (see notes).
R3: a separately named release under Phi.

A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method: an inventory of adapters plus a learned routing function. Adapters/LoRA are settled algorithm-side. Residue worth recording: the routing makes attributes=conditional-computation true of the fine-tuned model.

Episodic metric learning: a conv backbone plus a nearest-class-mean decision rule. The backbone is unchanged. Borderline -- it changes the prediction rule, not only the objective, so it is flagged in notes.

The released artifact is a protein-sequence tower plus a biomedical-text tower aligned in a shared space, i.e. the CLIP shape; R5 composite with the text encoder (PubMedBERT, admitted elsewhere in this file). The multimodal pretraining objective itself is algorithm-side. Low confidence: the paper calls ProtST a framework, which would make it algorithm-only.
R1+R3: a separately named domain-pretrained BERT release, exactly like BioBERT, SciBERT and ClinicalBERT, which are already nodes under BERT.
Quantile-regression distributional Q-learning; a change of learning target.
A causal meta-learner: a Neyman-orthogonal estimation strategy that composes arbitrary base models. Model-agnostic, so algorithm-side. See notes on the S/T/X/R-learner family.

Ambiguous referent and the quote does not disambiguate: optical-flow RAFT (Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms -- a lineage node, CNN encoder plus a GRU update operator over a correlation volume) versus Reward rAnked FineTuning (algorithm-side). `training RAFT on different datasets` fits either.
The same design named with its task. Strictly this is a fourth alias shape (task-suffixed form) that R3's three cases do not list -- see notes.
The episodic policy-gradient estimator; the quote uses it as the optimization procedure.
A causal meta-learner (single regression on features plus treatment). Model-agnostic estimation strategy, algorithm-side.
Soft Actor-Critic again, acronym-only. No lineage node exists to alias to, so the verdict is the algorithm verdict.

A cognitive process model of human decision making (sampling-based utility estimation), not a machine-learning architecture and not a training procedure for one. Neither the lineage root set nor the backbone test has anything to say about it. See notes: the corpus contains a class of domain simulation/process models the models dimension does not cover.

Masking-based speech separation: a learned convolutional encoder and decoder around a dual-path Transformer masker, hence the encoder-decoder pin. Dual-path chunking scores only intra- and inter-chunk pairs, which is sparse/local attention. CNN is a plausible R5 second parent for the learned front end.
A named shallow EEG-decoding convnet (Schirrmeister et al.), the companion of DeepConvNet, and a sibling of the existing EEGNet node.
Names a shape, not a release: two identical towers over two inputs compared at the end. The weight tying between towers -- the thing that makes it Siamese -- has no axis value (see notes).
A joint-embedding SSL objective with a stop-gradient; same class as BYOL and SimCLR.
Maximum-entropy RL objective; algorithm-side.
A self-tuning actor-critic variant of IMPALA driven by meta-gradients; a training procedure over an unchanged agent network.
A scalability-oriented DynGFN variant; inherits the GFlowNet verdict.
A causal meta-learner (two outcome models, one per treatment arm). Model-agnostic, algorithm-side.

A named binding-structure predictor: graph encoders for protein and ligand plus a trigonometry-aware interaction module predicting a distance map. The GNN edge is the best-supported one, but the paper's framing is about the trigonometry module and the pocket decomposition, so the parent is weak.
Self-described `the Thinker algorithm`: it wraps the environment in a learned world model and lets the agent plan in it; the agent network is unchanged.
An information-bottleneck training objective on directed information transfer; what is learned is a model whose architecture the method does not fix.

R5 hybrid, and the quote is the framing claim verbatim: `the first model that combines Transformer and U-Net`. Topology (encoder-decoder), convolution and the concatenative skips all come from U-Net; the new pin is self-attention in the encoder.

`a collection of vision models trained solely using a feature prediction objective` -- the released artifact is a ViT family, treated as MAE and DINOv2 are (L-18). The feature-prediction objective and the predictor are algorithm-side.
R1: MAE for video, framed directly against MAE, which is an existing node. Pins nothing new; the tube-masking scheme is an objective detail.
A causal meta-learner that builds on the T-learner's nuisance models; model-agnostic, algorithm-side.
